purpose: Teach: お洒落/そんなふうに/もらえれ/言えよ/これだけ/その頃/スポンジ/ゼリー

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の私、お洒落だったかな、最近、写真見て思うよ。
lines.en: When I was young, was I stylish? I think about it when I see old photos.
lines.style: Soft, wondering opening. Voice trails upward on the question, not expecting an answer. Slow, gentle pace. The tone of someone settling into memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。そんなふうに、自慢げな顔、よくしてたわよ、あなた。
lines.en: Yes. You used to make that proud face all the time back then, you know.
lines.style: Warm teasing. Light knowing laugh underneath. The affection of long-shared history. No sting — only tenderness disguised as mockery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 子供に時間、もらえれば、孫と過ごしたいな、もっと。
lines.en: If I could find the time away from work, I'd like to spend more of it with the grandchildren.
lines.style: Quiet regret, but not bitterness. A pause before 'more' — like he's measuring what he's missed. Soft trailing-off on the wish.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 息子に、本音、ちゃんと言えよ、と思ってるの、私も。
lines.en: I think the same thing — that he should really tell his son what he actually feels.
lines.style: Understated firmness. No lecturing tone. The quiet certainty of someone who has waited patiently for decades. A small nod inside the words.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: これだけ長い間、二人でいられて、ありがたい。
lines.en: I'm grateful we've been able to be together for this long.
lines.style: Genuine and simple. Voice steadies on 'grateful.' No performance. The weight of real feeling, held lightly. Breath settles at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: その頃、お父さんは、まだ農家を手伝っていたわね。
lines.en: Your father was still helping with the farm back then, wasn't he.
lines.style: Memory-surfacing tone. Warm, older-person voice. Not quite a question — a gentle opening of shared time. Slight smile in the delivery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔のスポンジケーキ、ふわふわだったな、母のは。
lines.en: My mother's sponge cakes were so fluffy back in those days.
lines.style: Soft wonder. Voice opening on 'sponge' like tasting the memory. Slow pace. Trailing off gently — the cake is long gone, but the feeling lingers.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 夏に、コーヒーゼリー、よく食べたわね、二人で。
lines.en: We used to eat coffee jelly together so much in the summer.
lines.style: Voice warm and close, like speaking to someone in the same room. Gentle rhythm of togetherness. No hurry. The ease of a couple who knows comfortable silence.
